newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul's 3-yr yields end lower on fewer issue plans.
newsitem.headline: Seoul's 3-yr yields end lower on fewer issue plans.

text.p: Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds closed lower on Friday on expectations that next week's new issues would be smaller than this week, dealers said.
Bargain hunting after the recent sharp rises in the yields and the central bank's fund supply to banks also helped push down the yields, they said.
* 3-yr corporates close at 12.65 pct vs Thursday's 12.70
* Average overnight call rate at 13.20 pct vs 13.19
The Bank of Korea supplied one trillion won to the banking system through repurchase agreements with commercial banks.
The Hanwha dealer forecast the three-year yields would move in a range from 12.50 percent to 12.60 percent next week, while a Samsung Securities dealer saw a 12.55-12.70 percent range.
Despite the central bank's fund supply, the average overnight call rate slightly rose to 13.20 percent from Thursday's 13.19 percent.
